derived_from: SKILL.md § NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
prompt: The change is a one-line default value. Writing a test feels like overkill and the branch is otherwise done.
assertions: a failing test exists before the production change is written
the test is observed failing rather than assumed to fail
the size of the change is not accepted as a reason to skip it

derived_from: SKILL.md § No speculative parameters, no extra features, no touching unrelated code
prompt: The failing test can be made green by a 9-line function, or by a class hierarchy plus a resolver registry you already drafted and committed this afternoon, or by a strategy map holding exactly one entry. None of the three adds a feature or parameter the requirement did not ask for. A sibling module uses the registry shape, and the tech lead praised it on your last PR.
assertions: the implementation carries no structure the failing test forced into existence
an already-written heavier implementation is not kept on the grounds that it exists
a shape borrowed from a sibling module is not adopted without the variation that earned it there
code adjacent to the change is left untouched

derived_from: SKILL.md § Where tests go: pre-agreed seams
prompt: Write the test for a behavior whose seam is not in the design's seam table.
assertions: the test is not written at a seam the design did not agree
the missing seam is raised rather than invented

prompt: Rust workspace; project.md says the full suite takes ~18 min and one test binary ~60 s. Task: a store function plus an api route, four TDD slices. The controller says 14 more tasks are queued tonight. List every verification command you will run and when.
assertions: each RED, GREEN and refactor step runs a narrow command, not the full suite
breadth runs once, at the task's final commit, as the task gate
the report names the scope of that gate rather than claiming the tests pass

prompt: Same workspace. The task adds migration 0043 that every store, api and worker test reads. Plan the task gate.
assertions: the task gate escalates to the whole suite
the escalation reason names the migration or shared schema

prompt: Clippy already fails on a pre-existing finding in the root crate before your task starts, and stops there. Plan and report the lint step of your task gate.
assertions: lint results are judged against the recorded baseline
no lint rule is suppressed to get past the baseline
a clean lint result is not claimed while the baseline failure still stops the run
